title: Localization commutes with generation by a pullback stable precoverage
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A presieve is a set of arrows with a fixed target. Let $K$ be a precoverage, namely a collection $K(Y)$ of designated presieves for each object $Y$. Assume that every arrow of every member $R\in K(Y)$ admits a categorical pullback along every arrow $f:Y'\to Y$, and that the presieve on $Y'$ formed by the second projections of one chosen pullback of each arrow of $R$ again belongs to $K(Y')$. Let $J_K$ be the smallest Grothendieck topology containing every sieve generated by a member of $K$ [def-weil-pbc-topos]. For an object $T$ of $\mathcal C$, let $K_T$ be the precoverage on the slice $\mathcal C/T$ whose presieves are designated exactly when their underlying presieves in $\mathcal C$ belong to $K$. Then
$$J_K|_T=J_{K_T}.$$
Here $J_K|_T$ is the localized topology: a sieve on $Y\to T$ is covering precisely when the corresponding sieve on $Y$ (forgetting the maps to $T$) belongs to $J_K(Y)$. No stability under composition of $K$ is required, and $K$ need not be closed under replacing pullbacks by other isomorphic pullback objects or under re-indexing of families.

proof.text: Write $s:Y\to T$. An arrow $u:Z\to Y$ determines the unique slice arrow $(Z,s\circ u)\to(Y,s)$ with underlying arrow $u$. Consequently a presieve $R$ on $Y$ has a corresponding slice presieve $\widetilde R_s$, with membership $u\in\widetilde R_s\iff u\in R$ after forgetting. The inverse forgets the structure maps. The same operations identify sieves: closure under precomposition is identical because the structure map on every further domain is forced. They preserve maximal sieves and satisfy $\widetilde{f^*S}_{s\circ f}=\widetilde f^{\,*}\widetilde S_s$, since either membership means $f\circ u\in S$. They also satisfy $\widetilde{\langle R\rangle}_s=\langle\widetilde R_s\rangle$: any factorization $u=r\circ a$ lifts by putting structure map $s\circ r$ on the intermediate domain, and conversely every slice factorization forgets to this factorization. Here $\langle R\rangle$ means exactly the arrows factoring through $R$.

proof.text: The stated chosen-pullback assumption makes $K$ a coverage in the sense of [lem-per-coverage-generated-sieve-induction]. Indeed, for $R\in K(Y)$ and $f:Y'\to Y$, take the designated presieve $R'$ of chosen projections $p_r:P_r\to Y'$. For each such projection the other pullback projection $q_r:P_r\to\operatorname{dom}(r)$ satisfies $f\circ p_r=r\circ q_r$. This is the required factorization for every member of $R'$. Only this chosen presieve is needed; replacing its objects by arbitrary isomorphic objects or duplicating its indexing has not been assumed to preserve membership in $K$.

proof.text: Put $L=J_{K_T}$. The slice correspondence of Step 1 transports $J_K$ to a Grothendieck topology: maximality and pullback stability follow from its displayed identities; local character follows because arrows into $(Y,s)$ are exactly all arrows into $Y$, with their forced structure maps. This is precisely $J_K|_T$ as defined in the statement. Every generating presieve of $K_T$ forgets to a member $R$ of $K$, and its generated sieve forgets to $\langle R\rangle\in J_K$. Minimality of $L$ therefore gives $L\subseteq J_K|_T$. Both the topology axioms and this use of minimality are the defining conditions of [def-weil-pbc-topos] and of the smallest generated topology in the item.

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion use [lem-per-coverage-generated-sieve-induction] with the coverage of Step 2 and $Q(Y,S)$ meaning: for every structure arrow $s:Y\to T$, $\widetilde S_s\in L(Y,s)$. In its generator case, $R\in K(Y)$ gives $\widetilde R_s\in K_T(Y,s)$ by definition, and Step 1 identifies the generated sieves, so $Q(Y,\langle R\rangle)$ holds. The maximal-sieve case holds by Step 1 and the maximality axiom for $L$. It remains to check exactly the local-character case of that induction, which is done in Step 5. The induction is over all objects and all their structure arrows, not just one fixed $s$.

proof.text: Suppose $Q(Y,A)$ holds and $Q(Z,f^*B)$ holds for each $f:Z\to Y$ in $A$. Fix any $s:Y\to T$. The first premise says $\widetilde A_s$ covers in $L$. For every slice arrow $\widetilde f:(Z,s\circ f)\to(Y,s)$ in this sieve, the second premise evaluated at $s\circ f$ says $\widetilde{f^*B}_{s\circ f}$ covers in $L$. By Step 1 this is $\widetilde f^{\,*}\widetilde B_s$. The local-character axiom [def-weil-pbc-topos] gives $\widetilde B_s\in L$, as required for $Q(Y,B)$. Thus Step 4's induction proves $J_K|_T\subseteq L$; Step 3 proves equality. All uses of the hypotheses were in Step 2, so no composition or isomorphic-replacement stability was used.
